title: CPC Week-2 hazard outlooks (CONUS, 2017-2026): cold risk levels agree per day, but heavy-precipitation Moderate and High verified at 0.29 and 0.37, as the 1-inch criterion fails in dry areas
abstract: Question: are the risk levels of the NOAA CPC Week-2 (days 8-14) probabilistic hazards outlook calibrated, and which part of the forecast or of the hazard definition causes any error? CPC states slight 20-40%, moderate 40-60% and high more than 60%. Approach: pre-registered test of all archived probabilistic polygons for much-below-normal temperature (2019-2026) and heavy precipitation (2017-2026) over CONUS (1,343 and 3,312 polygons), with the CPC nominal criteria (cold: Tmin below the 1991-2020 15th percentile and at or below 35 F; heavy precipitation: 3-day total above the 85th percentile and above 1 inch) on CPC gridded analyses, frequency per valid day, month-block bootstrap. Post hoc: criterion-part decomposition, lead time inside polygons, 543 GHCN-Daily first-order stations. Results: cold risks were calibrated per day (0.30, 0.51, 0.74), but their any-day frequencies were 0.59-0.87, and unflagged land within 200 km of cold polygons had 0.21-0.62, so the cold areas are drawn too small. Heavy-precipitation moderate (0.29 [0.25, 0.32]) and high (0.37 [0.27, 0.51]) failed; slight was at its floor (0.19 [0.18, 0.21]). Stations agreed (0.31, 0.45). The percentile part alone verified at the stated levels (grid 0.39 and 0.55; stations 0.40 and 0.61). The 1-inch part removed the events: in the 24-33% of moderate and high area where the local 85th percentile is well below 1 inch (61% west of 100 W), the hazard occurred in 13-14% of 3-day windows. A second part: frequency fell from the first to the last window of a polygon (high 0.46 to 0.25; paired -0.32 [-0.46, -0.16]), while cold showed no fall. Exceedance of the 1991-2020 temperature percentiles drifted (Tmax above P85 on 18-27% of days in 2020-2026). Limitations: CPC criteria are guidelines that forecasters may change; 35 F and day conventions are our choices; the warm hazard sample (105 polygons) is too small; heat, snow and wind were not tested; Alaska excluded; few months for high levels.
